title: Residual-VQ Mirror code composition for logical linear functions
hypothesis: On the same rank-four function bank as MA-481, train-only residual VQ at K=8 or 16 and 2/3/4 stages will improve the heldout function-quality/byte frontier over single-stage VQ, with at least one config achieving RMSE <=0.05, >=0.90 unique heldout address tuples, and <=6,101 actual serialized bytes in both development seeds.
physical_object: four shared 16x16 matrix atoms fitted on 128 functions
mirror_coordinate: ordered tuple of residual-VQ stage indices selecting a sum of residual latent code vectors
logical_multiplicity: 192 callable linear functions; 128 train and 64 heldout

task.fit: SVD on training matrices; each residual codebook fitted by train-only Euclidean k-means with 100 Lloyd steps; heldout coordinates encoded stagewise using frozen codebooks

selection_metrics: fit/decode/query wall time and operation proxies

paid_objects: one index per function per stage
codebook/stage schema and function ordering metadata

compute.query: Every function uses the same 64 queries within each world. Matrix evaluation charges D^2 MACs; decoding sums all stage latent vectors then applies shared atoms. Fit includes SVD and all train-only k-means iterations; report heldout address encoding/query separately.

gates.PROMISING: At least one residual-VQ configuration in both seeds has RMSE <=0.05, unique heldout address tuples >=0.90, complete payload <=6,101 bytes and exact replay; this is only a residual-VQ quality-rate result. No Mirror-specific claim if the native RVQ serializer aliases it.
gates.FAIL: Independent upper is valid, but no residual config satisfies the quality/uniqueness/byte gate, or residual VQ exactly aliases native RVQ for Mirror-specific attribution.
gates.NOT ESTABLISHED: Independent upper fails to reproduce targets or serialization/metric replay fails.

boundaries: Synthetic rank-four linear bank only; not a trained language model or natural task set.
Nominal code sequence count is not independent function capacity; heldout output behavior and address collisions decide.
Fresh worlds remain sealed unless frozen feasibility gates pass; native RVQ attribution is reported separately.
